root_idea.summary: The root denotes inclination, bending, and curvature.
root_idea.development: From the idea of bending or curving come the noun حِقْف for a curved or sloping sand tract and its plural أَحْقَاف, as well as derived descriptions of curved forms in animals and other objects.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the supported singular lexical citation form حِقْف; the Quranic occurrence is its plural proper-name form أَحْقَاف.

senses.definition: Curved or sloping sand tracts; in the Qur'an, al-Aḥqāf is the place-name for such a sand region.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence uses the plural أَحْقَاف as a geographical proper name. It is the plural of حِقْف, a curved or sloping tract of sand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become curved, bent, or winding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same curved or curled state is applied to a gazelle described as حَاقِفٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assume a long, curved, bent, or winding form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of sand, the narrow visible rim of the moon near the sun, a back including a camel's back, or other things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lower or lowest part of a tract of sand, a mountain, or a wall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a topographical sense distinct from حِقْف as a curved sand tract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gazelle lying bent together or curled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The posture may occur in sleep or as a result of a wound; the term also applies to one lying on its breast upon a حِقْف of sand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lank in the belly, said of a camel.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Form I curvature meaning and its curled-gazelle application are covered.
The derived verb's long, curved-form meaning is covered.
The curved sand-tract meaning and its regional plural application are covered.
The lower-part topographical meaning is separately represented.

cautions: The Quranic form is tagged as a proper noun and appears in the plural أَحْقَاف; it is presented under the lexically supported singular citation form حِقْف.
